disclaimer: This report is for educational and wellness purposes only. It is not a medical diagnosis and does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. HbA1c results should be confirmed by your doctor. Do not start, stop or change any medication without medical advice.

status.label: In the normal range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over roughly the last 2–3 months and is below the 5.7% threshold used for prediabetes.

summary: Your HbA1c of 5.3% is in the normal range, which is great news. Your BMI of 22.7 also falls in the normal category, and you're very active, which supports healthy blood sugar levels. The main risk factor to address is current smoking, which can affect blood vessels and long-term metabolic health. Keeping up with regular HbA1c and blood pressure checks, staying active, and working toward quitting smoking are the most valuable next steps for protecting your health.

Lean proteins such as chicken, turkey, fish, and eggs
Low-fat dairy like Greek yogurt and cottage cheese
foods_to_avoid: Processed meats high in sodium like bacon and salami
plan.portion_guidance: Since your calorie target is 2,900 kcal and you are very active, meals are larger than average with extra whole grains and protein to support your activity level. Use your palm size for protein portions, a cupped handful for grains, and fill at least a third of your plate with vegetables at lunch and dinner.
plan.hydration: Aim for about 3 to 3.5 liters of water across the day, more on days with intense training. Limit sugary sports drinks unless you are doing very long or intense sessions, and keep alcohol occasional as you already do.
based_on: current smoker: emphasis on antioxidant-rich vegetables and fruits
occasional alcohol: moderate intake guidance included

exercise: You're already very active, which is great. Keep up at least 150 minutes a week of moderate activity, or continue your current higher level if that feels comfortable.
Add muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days a week, working major muscle groups like legs, back, chest and arms.
Mix in variety such as cycling, swimming or sports to keep things enjoyable and reduce overuse strain.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Aim for at least 30 minutes of brisk walking on 5 days a week. Since you're already very active, you can start right at this level or use it as a warm-up or recovery activity alongside your other exercise.
lifestyle.weight_management: Your BMI is in the normal range, so the focus should be on maintaining your current weight through balanced eating and staying active, rather than losing weight.
lifestyle.sleep: Aim for 7 to 9 hours of sleep each night. Try to go to bed and wake up at the same time each day, keep your bedroom cool and dark, and avoid screens for 30 to 60 minutes before bed.
stress: Try deep breathing exercises for a few minutes each day, especially during stressful moments.
Consider regular mindfulness or meditation practice, even just 10 minutes a day, using a free app or guided audio.
Make time for hobbies or activities you enjoy to help you unwind.
behaviour_change: Since you currently smoke, quitting is one of the best things you can do for your long-term health. Consider calling a quitline for free support and coaching.
Talk to your doctor about support options and strategies that can help you quit successfully.
Set a quit date and tell friends or family for extra accountability and encouragement.
Since you drink occasionally, keep an eye on your overall intake and stick to recommended limits to support your health goals.

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Regular screening finds changes before symptoms appear.
monitoring.frequency: Every 3 years, or yearly if your doctor advises because of risk factors

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Consider resources or support programs to help reduce or quit smoking, since it can affect blood vessel health and blood sugar regulation over time
Keep up your very active lifestyle with regular physical activity most days of the week
Maintain a balanced diet that supports your 2900 calorie target without needing special restrictions right now
Schedule routine HbA1c and blood pressure checks to catch any changes early
Limit alcohol to occasional use as you're already doing, to support overall metabolic health

hba1c_caveat: HbA1c can be less accurate if you have anaemia, kidney disease, a recent blood transfusion or certain haemoglobin variants.
